newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam rice market firm, but export deals slow.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam rice market firm, but export deals slow.

text.p: Vietnam's rice market was firmer this week, with shipments from Saigon Port continuing at a steady pace, but dealers said exports looked set to slow in the weeks ahead.
Dealers forecast June's exports at 450,000-500,000 tonnes, taking the total since the beginning of this year to around 1.8 million tonnes.
Traders, however, saw exports dropping to 300,000-400,000 tonnes next month due to slowing demand and stockpiling of quality rice by farmers in the Mekong Delta.
Annual flooding in the delta usually means the summer-autumn harvest is smaller and of a lower quality, so farmers hold winter-spring paddy back to mix with the later crop.
Recent port congestion appeared to be easing, with 23 vessels -- mostly bound for Africa -- loading compared with more than 30 earlier in the month.
Traders put the price of five-percent broken grade, FOB Saigon Port, at $255-$260 per tonne compared with $255 last week, and 10-percent at $250-$253 a tonne, up from $247-$250.
